the radiative heat flux to the fuel is dependent on the heater type and the operating temperature and that the spectral behavior of the heaters is different, which affects the in-depth absorption.
the heater type and temperature have significant effects on the radiative transfer in the translucent fuel, and the spectral heterogeneity of the fuel absorption coefficient is large.

the radiative heat absorption of a translucent fuel sample and the influence of the heating source.
the fundamental mechanisms of radiative heat absorption in the translucent fuel samples and provides a solid base for the future development of a multi-band fire radiation model.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the radiative heat exchange between a solid and a blackbody is independent of the solid thickness.

the spectral radiative heat transfer to translucent fuel should be calculated using a multi-band model and the spectral transmittance of the material should be measured over the whole wavelength range encountered in fires.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a translucent fuel sample should not be considered as a blackbody, and that the heater type should be taken into account for radiative heat exchange.
the radiative heat flux is not a simple function of the heater operating temperature, but it is also dependent on the spectral characteristics of the heater.

the radiative transfer in translucent fuel is a complex process and that the radiative heat fluxes to the sample depend on the source spectral distribution, the heater operating temperature, the sample thickness and the material properties.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the radiative heat exchange is a complex process that cannot be simplified by the common assumption of greybody behavior and Beer–Lamberts’s law.
a multi-band radiation transfer model is necessary to accurately predict radiative heat transfer and hence the pyrolisis process for translucent fuels.
the spectral properties of the heaters and of the sample are important and must be taken into account to accurately model the radiative heat fluxes to a translucent solid.
